notes.scope: B2C E-Commerce Platform MVP — 7 backend services + Next.js frontend (identity, catalog, inventory, cart, checkout, order, payment, frontend-web). Refactored by Tech-Lead in dry-run #2 from the dry-run #1 baseline. Closes REV-L2-001 (buyerEmail dataflow), REV-L2-002 (canonical INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET env-var name), and REV-L2-003 (constant-time secret comparison) at the contracts level.
locked_decisions_summary: Persistence: PostgreSQL via common/database (pgx). Schema-per-service. No cross-service tables.
Route convention: POST /api/v1/{domain}/{aggregate-boundary}/{action} (revised from go-template's /api/v1/platform/{domain}/{action}; the 'platform' segment is dropped, '{aggregate-boundary}' added).

Auth (LOCKED): JWT ES256 via common/token for end-user/customer + admin authentication. Internal service-to-service authentication uses a single shared secret named INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET (no other env-var name accepted; see cross-cutting.auth.internal_service_auth). All recipients MUST compare the supplied X-Internal-Secret value against the configured secret using crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare; plain '==' / '!=' is forbidden and is a high-severity reviewer finding. Closes REV-L2-002 and REV-L2-003.

Response envelope: {code, message, data, traceId} per common/wrapper.Response[T]. TraceID is automatically taken from gin-context key wrapper.CtxTraceID (set by middleware.TraceContextTraceIDMiddleware) when the handler omits it. Resolves the BA-flagged conflict against requirement §14; orchestrator-locked envelope wins.

Stock reservation atomicity (LOCKED): Synchronous orchestration — Checkout calls inventory.reservation.create over HTTP inside a single Checkout-side transaction guarding the Order row; Inventory uses a row-level lock per SKU (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) inside its own DB transaction. Failure to reserve aborts Order creation. Post-payment commit/release is event-driven (see §async events) via Kafka with the Outbox pattern from Payment + Order so the bus is reliable. Tradeoff: HTTP coupling at checkout-time, but transactionally tight; outbox absorbs Kafka unavailability post-payment.

Inventory lock-order (LOCKED): for any tx that locks more than one stock_levels row, locks MUST be acquired in ascending sku string order. inventory.reservation.create sorts items by sku before iterating SELECT ... FOR UPDATE. inventory.reservation.commit, .release, and .sweep-expired only ever touch a single sku per row, so they cannot deadlock — but documented here for the bulk-reservation path.

Payment callback idempotency (LOCKED): idempotency key = (paymentIntentId, providerStatus). Persisted in payment.callback_dedup table with the request-body hash + result snapshot. Window = until intent's terminal state retention (>= 30 days). Duplicate that arrives after stock-committed returns 200 with the original result envelope; never re-emits domain events.

Order state machine ownership (LOCKED): Order service is sole writer of order.status. Payment service NEVER writes order rows directly. Payment publishes payment.completed | payment.failed | payment.expired events; Order consumes and transitions. Inventory consumes the same events for reservation-commit / reservation-release.

Cart→Order boundary (LOCKED): Cart 'becomes' an Order at the moment checkout.commit succeeds and Order is created in PENDING_PAYMENT. Items moved into the order are removed from the cart in the same Checkout transaction (CHK-010). Other cart items remain.

Frontend↔backend topology (LOCKED): Direct-to-services through thin Next.js Route Handlers acting as auth-cookie→Authorization-header proxies. NO dedicated BFF service. Each service is reachable behind a gateway path; frontend never holds the JWT in JavaScript — refresh token is HttpOnly cookie, access token cached in memory by the route handler per request. Frontend MUST NEVER forward the X-Internal-Secret header or load INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET into its environment.

buyerEmail dataflow (LOCKED — REV-L2-001 fix): Checkout fetches the customer's email via identity.profile.read (Bearer JWT, customer's own access token) inside checkout.commit step 2 and includes it as buyerEmail in the order.create-from-checkout request. Order persists buyerEmailSnapshot on order_items snapshot block so admin order search by email (order.list-admin) works after the fact and customer-facing orderDetail does not have to round-trip identity. identity.profile.read is in the contracts list as a first-class customer-JWT contract, NOT a stub.

fields.message: string (human-readable; localized later, English in MVP)
fields.data: object|array|null (handler-specific success payload; null on error)
fields.traceId: string (W3C-traceparent-derived; non-empty on every response, success or error)

payload_shape.applies_to: every JSON response from every HTTP endpoint, success or error

failure_modes: Handler returns wrapper.Respond with a non-CodeSuccess code → HTTP status mapped per cross-cutting.error-codes
Middleware-level panic → wrapper emits CodeInternalError envelope with traceId derived from middleware.TraceContextTraceIDMiddleware

payload_shape.refresh_token_format: JWT signed ES256 via common/token (separate keypair allowed; longer expiry)
payload_shape.transport: Authorization: Bearer <jwt> on every authenticated request. Frontend Next.js route handlers (which are STATELESS per-request — there is no shared in-memory cache across requests) acquire the access token freshly each call via the per-request flow described in token_acquisition_flow below.

cookies.access: HttpOnly cookie 'access' — value is the access JWT (tokenType=ACCESS); attributes: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Max-Age = access_token_expiry (15 min suggested)
cookies.refresh: HttpOnly cookie 'refresh' — value is the refresh JWT (tokenType=REFRESH); attributes: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Max-Age = refresh_token_expiry (14 days suggested)

per_request_steps: 1. Route handler reads the 'access' cookie from the incoming request.

2. If 'access' is present AND not expired (decode header.payload locally, check exp claim against now() with a small 30s skew tolerance) → forward Authorization: Bearer <access> to the downstream service. Return its response.
3. If 'access' is absent OR expired → read the 'refresh' cookie. If absent, respond 401 AUTH_MISSING.
4. Call identity.refresh with {refreshToken: <refresh-cookie-value>}. On 200, the response carries a NEW access token AND a NEW (rotated) refresh token; the old refresh-jti is revoked server-side.
5. Set-Cookie both cookies with rotated values (same attributes), then forward the original request as Bearer <new-access> to downstream.
6. On identity.refresh AUTH_INVALID/AUTH_REVOKED → clear both cookies (Max-Age=0) and respond 401 AUTH_REVOKED to the browser; the SPA must redirect to login.
token_acquisition_flow.rotation_guarantee: Each successful identity.refresh issues a new refresh token AND revokes the old refresh-jti (single-use rotation). A replay of the old refresh-cookie outside the 5s soft-idempotency window returns AUTH_REVOKED.
token_acquisition_flow.no_javascript_access: Neither cookie is readable from JavaScript (HttpOnly). The frontend SPA never sees the JWT bytes; auth state is inferred from a separate, non-sensitive 'auth-hint' cookie (or a /me probe) for UI gating.

payload_shape.middleware_behavior: common/middleware JWT middleware (on the BACKEND services) validates signature (ES256), iss, aud, exp; on success injects token.Claims into context via token.WithClaims; on failure responds 401 AUTH_INVALID with envelope.
payload_shape.role_rejection_rules: Admin-only endpoints check claims.role == ADMIN; if CUSTOMER, respond 403 AUTH_FORBIDDEN. Public endpoints skip the JWT middleware entirely (registered outside the protected route group).
payload_shape.access_token_expiry: 15 minutes (suggested; identity service config; must be < refresh expiry)
payload_shape.logout_behavior: identity.logout writes the refresh-token jti into a revoked-jti store (Redis with TTL = remaining exp). Refresh attempts with a revoked jti respond 401 AUTH_REVOKED.

internal_service_auth.scope: Authentication for service-to-service HTTP calls inside the cluster (Checkout→Inventory, Checkout→Order, Checkout→Payment, Order→Payment cancel-on-failure). Customer/Admin requests use JWT (above); never both.
internal_service_auth.header: X-Internal-Secret: <secret> on every internal call; the absence of this header on an internal-protected route is 401 AUTH_INVALID.
internal_service_auth.env_var_name: INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET (LOCKED — no other name accepted; e.g. INTERNAL_SECRET, SHARED_SECRET, SVC_SECRET are all rejected at startup with a fatal config error). All four caller/recipient services (checkout, order, inventory, payment) MUST read this exact env-var name. Closes REV-L2-002.
internal_service_auth.value_format: ASCII string, MIN 32 bytes (256 bits of entropy). Recipient services MUST validate length at startup and refuse to boot if shorter — this prevents accidental empty-string acceptance (REV-L2-002 footnote) and trivially-short values.
internal_service_auth.comparison_rule: Recipient services MUST use crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(supplied), []byte(secret)) == 1 to validate the supplied header value. Plain Go == / != string comparison is FORBIDDEN — short-circuit byte-by-byte compare leaks the secret over a timing oracle (CWE-208 / OWASP API2:2023 / ASVS V2.4.7). Closes REV-L2-003.
internal_service_auth.shared_helper: Recipient services SHOULD import a single shared helper (recommended path: backend/common/middleware/internal_auth.go) so the constant-time-compare pattern, audit-log line, and rotation-overlap support live in one place. Inlined per-service implementations are permitted in MVP only if each one provably uses subtle.ConstantTimeCompare; Reviewer-L1 / Reviewer-L2 scan for plain '==' / '!=' on this header.
internal_service_auth.rotation_overlap: INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET MAY accept a comma-separated value (new,old) so an operator can roll the secret across all four services without a synchronized restart. Recipient services try ConstantTimeCompare against each comma-segment; first match wins. Single-value configurations remain valid.
internal_service_auth.frontend_does_not_use: The Next.js frontend MUST NOT forward X-Internal-Secret to backend services and MUST NOT load INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET into its env (frontend/.env.example explicitly omits it). Customer-originated requests reach backend services as Bearer JWT only. A frontend regression test asserts the absence of X-Internal-Secret on customer-originated requests.
internal_service_auth.audit_logging: On every reject, the recipient service logs slog.Error with msg='internal_auth_reject', remoteAddr, x_forwarded_for, path, requestId. NEVER logs the supplied or expected secret value. On startup, every recipient service logs slog.Info with msg='internal_auth_configured' and sha256_prefix=hex(sha256(secret))[:8] so ops can confirm at a glance that all four services hash the same secret without ever logging the secret itself.

contracts.idempotency_rules: n/a (token issuance is non-idempotent by design — every login produces a fresh access+refresh pair). Refresh endpoint MAY be idempotent within a 5s rolling window keyed by refresh jti to absorb client-side retries.
failure_modes: AUTH_MISSING — no Authorization header on protected endpoint (HTTP 401)
AUTH_INVALID — internal-protected endpoint received a request with missing or wrong X-Internal-Secret (HTTP 401); recipient logs internal_auth_reject; never logs the supplied or expected secret value

payload_shape.header: Idempotency-Key: <client-supplied opaque string, max 128 chars, UUID recommended>
payload_shape.applies_to: checkout.commit (CHK-009), inventory.reservation.create (server-side internal — keyed on orderId), order.create-from-checkout (server-side internal — keyed on orderId), payment.intent.create (server-side internal — keyed on orderId), payment.callback (server-side internal — keyed on (paymentIntentId, providerStatus))

server_side_store.schema: idempotency_keys table per service: {key (PK, scoped per endpoint), request_hash (sha256 of canonicalized body), response_envelope (jsonb), http_status (int), created_at, expires_at}
server_side_store.ttl: 24 hours for checkout.commit; 30 days for payment.callback (>= retention horizon for payment-provider redelivery)
server_side_store.scope: per-(endpoint, customerUserId) for checkout; per-(paymentIntentId, providerStatus) for payment.callback; per-orderId for inventory.reservation.create / order.create-from-checkout / payment.intent.create

behavior.first_call: Process normally; persist (key, request_hash, response_envelope) inside the same DB transaction that commits the business write — atomic.
behavior.duplicate_same_payload: Return the persisted response_envelope verbatim (same status, same body). Do NOT re-execute side-effects.
behavior.duplicate_different_payload: Return 409 with code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED + the originally created resource id. Do NOT honor the new payload.

payload_shape.internal_orderId_rule: LOCKED (closes REV-L2-006): Any internal call derived from checkout.commit (steps 6/7/8 in checkout.commit.internal_orchestration) MUST set Idempotency-Key == the new orderId UUID v7. Recipients (Inventory.reservation.create, Order.create-from-checkout, Payment.intent.create) MUST validate idempotencyKey == request.orderId at the handler boundary and return 400 VALIDATION_ERROR if they differ. The customer-facing Idempotency-Key on POST /checkout/checkout/commit is a SEPARATE scope (per-(endpoint, customerUserId) in Checkout's local DB) and is never forwarded downstream — Checkout substitutes orderId at the boundary.

failure_modes: IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INFLIGHT — concurrent call with same key while first is still executing (HTTP 409 with Retry-After: 1; client retries)
VALIDATION_ERROR — internal call's Idempotency-Key != orderId on a route that requires the orderId-keyed rule (HTTP 400)

payload_shape.convention: Codes are SCREAMING_SNAKE. New codes must be added to this registry (a contract bump) before use; Tech-Designers may not invent codes.
payload_shape.ba_flagged_resolution: AUTH-007: identity.login returns the SAME code+message for invalid email and invalid password — 'AUTH_INVALID' / 'Invalid email or password.' This is the locked phrasing.

failure_modes: Tech-Designer references a code not in the registry → Plan-Reviewer or QA-L1 must reject

payload_shape.rationale: Verb-in-body, action in path. Mirrors go-template's POST-only style but drops 'platform' and adds an explicit aggregate-boundary segment so domain services that own multiple aggregates (e.g. identity owns user + address) keep clean URL grouping.
trailing_rules: List-style queries are POST with body filters — paging via {page, limit}; sort via {sort: 'price_asc'|...}.

Internal service-to-service calls use the same routes; no separate /internal prefix in MVP. Authorization is tightened via reserved internal-service JWTs (separate ADMIN-like role 'SERVICE') in a future iteration; in MVP, internal calls flow over a private network plane.

failure_modes: Tech-Designer omits {aggregate-boundary} or invents a verb segment → Plan-Reviewer rejects

payload_shape.schema_layout: One database per service (or one Postgres instance with one schema per service in MVP local Docker Compose). Each service OWNS its tables. NO cross-service joins. NO shared tables.
schemas_listing: inventory: stock_levels (sku PK, available_qty, reserved_qty, sold_qty, version), reservations (id, order_id, sku, qty, expires_at, status), stock_adjustments (delta, reason, actor_user_id, created_at)
checkout: idempotency_keys (key, customer_user_id, request_hash, response_envelope, expires_at) — checkout DOES NOT own orders or payments; it orchestrates
order: orders, order_items (with priceSnapshot, productNameSnapshot, productImageUrlSnapshot), order_status_history, order_addresses (snapshot), outbox_events
payment: payment_intents, payment_records (mockPaymentRef, providerStatus, paidAt), callback_dedup, outbox_events
transactional_boundaries: checkout.commit: SINGLE Postgres transaction in checkout's idempotency_keys store + a SYNC HTTP call to inventory.reservation.create (which uses ITS OWN local FOR UPDATE tx) + a SYNC HTTP call to order.create-from-checkout (single tx writing orders + order_items + order_status_history + outbox PENDING_PAYMENT event) + a SYNC HTTP call to payment.intent.create (single tx writing payment_intents). On any sync-call failure, checkout calls inventory.reservation.release as compensation, then surfaces error to client. Net effect: at-most-one Order, at-most-one reservation, at-most-one intent.

inventory.reservation.commit (event-driven from payment.completed): single tx inside inventory: SELECT stock FOR UPDATE, decrement reserved, increment sold, mark reservation COMMITTED, write to inventory outbox if needed. Idempotent on (reservation_id, COMMITTED).
inventory.reservation.release (event-driven from payment.failed | payment.expired | order.cancelled): single tx, opposite of commit. Idempotent.
payment.callback: single tx in payment: dedup-check, then write payment_records + outbox payment.completed | payment.failed | payment.expired event. Order + Inventory consume from Kafka.

outbox_pattern.shape: table outbox_events {id (uuid v7), aggregate_id, event_type, payload_json, created_at, published_at NULL}
outbox_pattern.publisher: in-process goroutine polls outbox_events WHERE published_at IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 100, sends to Kafka via common/kafka, marks published_at; at-least-once
outbox_pattern.consumer_idempotency: consumers must dedupe on event_id (UUID v7 in payload header)

payload_shape.migrations: each service owns its migrations under /migrations/*.sql (golang-migrate or sqlx-style); applied at service startup if MIGRATIONS_AUTO_APPLY=true (local/dev only) — manual in UAT/PROD.
concurrency: stock_levels uses optimistic version column AND SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the row inside reservation/commit/release transactions — belt and suspenders (the FOR UPDATE is the binding mechanism; version is a defensive check).
Negative-quantity invariant enforced via CHECK constraints: CHECK (available_qty >= 0 AND reserved_qty >= 0 AND sold_qty >= 0).

failure_modes: DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE — Postgres unreachable; service returns 503 with envelope (NF: failure_tolerance)
Outbox publisher lag — no client-visible failure; events catch up; consumers must be idempotent
contracts.ordering_guarantees: Outbox publisher is single-threaded per service → preserves per-aggregate event order at the producer. Kafka partition key (see per-event contracts) preserves it on consumer side.

payload_shape.scope: Canonical server-side pricing formula for checkout.preview and checkout.commit. Authoritative; the cart's informational subtotal does NOT bind.

formula.subtotal: sum(orderItem.priceSnapshot * orderItem.qty) over all checkoutable items (PRODUCT_INACTIVE/PRODUCT_DELETED/INSUFFICIENT_STOCK lines excluded from the order entirely — see checkout.preview.blockers / checkout.commit.failure_modes)
formula.shippingFee: Tier rule per requirement §11.2: subtotal < 1500 THB → shippingFee = 60 THB; subtotal >= 1500 THB → shippingFee = 0 THB. Boundary is inclusive at 1500 (i.e. exactly 1500 → free shipping).
formula.couponDiscount: 0 in this run. Coupon engine is out_of_scope; the field is reserved for future iterations and is documented as 0 wherever shippingFee is documented.
formula.grandTotal: subtotal + shippingFee - couponDiscount  ==  subtotal + shippingFee  (in this run, since couponDiscount=0)

payload_shape.currency: THB only in MVP. All amounts are decimal-safe (server uses int64 minor units or shopspring/decimal; never float64). API surface uses 'number' representing whole-THB integers (no fractional THB in MVP).
payload_shape.applies_to: checkout.preview.response_data, checkout.commit.response_data, order.detail.response_data (subtotal/total fields persisted on order_items + orders at commit-time and immutable thereafter)

failure_modes: VALIDATION_ERROR — subtotal < 0 (defensive; should be unreachable since per-line lineSubtotal is a non-negative integer)
contracts.notes: Resolves PR-002 (BA repair §11.2) ↔ TL alignment. checkout.preview.shippingFee and checkout.commit.shippingFee MUST reference this formula. RESERVATION_TTL_MINUTES is centralized here so inventory.reservation.create's expiresAt suggestion (now+15min) and inventory.reservation.sweep-expired's scan window stay in lockstep.

contracts.idempotency_rules: Not idempotent. Repeat with same email returns 409 DUPLICATE_EMAIL.
failure_modes: VALIDATION_ERROR — bad email format, password too short, name empty

contracts.idempotency_rules: Not idempotent (each call mints fresh tokens).
failure_modes: AUTH_INVALID — wrong email OR wrong password; SAME code+message for both (AUTH-007 locked)

contracts.idempotency_rules: Soft-idempotent: same refreshToken submitted twice within 5s rolling window returns same response (single-use rotation otherwise). Reuse outside window returns AUTH_REVOKED.
failure_modes: AUTH_REVOKED — refresh jti previously consumed or logout-revoked

contracts.idempotency_rules: Idempotent on refresh-jti: second logout for the same jti returns 200 with revoked=true.

payload_shape.request: {} (userId from claims.sub on the customer's own access token)

response_data.email: string (immutable in MVP; load-bearing for buyerEmail snapshot — see callers)
response_data.name: string

contracts.callers: (1) frontend-web profile route (display-only); (2) checkout.commit step 2 — Checkout pulls the customer's email here using the customer's own Bearer JWT (same auth context the request arrived with — Checkout forwards the incoming Authorization header) and stores it as buyerEmail on the order.create-from-checkout request. This is a Phase-1 first-class contract, NOT a stub. Closes REV-L2-001 (the dry-run #1 buyerEmail dataflow gap that broke every checkout at order.create-from-checkout binding).
contracts.notes: Identity is NOT permitted to put email into the access JWT extra claims to satisfy this dataflow — keeping email out of the JWT minimizes blast radius of token leakage and preserves AUTH-007 generic login error semantics. The HTTP round-trip cost is acceptable because checkout.commit is already a multi-call orchestration and the Identity DB lookup is sub-10ms on an indexed PK.

contracts.idempotency_rules: Last-writer-wins on (name, phone). No idempotency key required.

request.isDefault: boolean (optional; if true, demotes the prior default in the same tx)

contracts.idempotency_rules: Idempotent: deleting an already-deleted address returns 200 deleted=true.
Idempotent — re-setting the same default is a no-op success.

response_data.items: Product[] (only ACTIVE; hides DRAFT/INACTIVE/DELETED — CAT-001, CAT-010)

failure_modes: VALIDATION_ERROR (page<1, limit out of range, bad sort enum)
contracts.ordering_guarantees: Server-side stable sort by (sort_key, productId) so pagination is deterministic.
contracts.notes: When inStock=true, catalog calls inventory.stock.bulk-read for the candidate productIds and filters server-side. This is a sync inter-service call; catalog must tolerate inventory unavailable → 503.

response_data.name: string
response_data.stockStatus: string (enum: IN_STOCK | LOW | OUT_OF_STOCK; computed by joining inventory)

failure_modes: PRODUCT_DELETED (still resolvable for admin and historical-order paths; for guest/customer storefront returns NOT_FOUND)

contracts.side_effects: Catalog publishes product.created event on outbox. Inventory consumes and seeds stock_levels(sku) with all-zero quantities. Until inventory has seeded the SKU, listing with inStock=true filters this product out.

failure_modes: DUPLICATE_SKU (if sku editable; locked: NOT editable in MVP)
contracts.side_effects: Records change in product_status_history (CAT-008). Publishes product.updated event.

contracts.notes: Storefront listing/detail filters out DELETED. Order detail still resolves snapshot fields stored on order_items (CAT-009).

request.activeOnly: boolean? (default true for storefront, false for admin)

contracts.callers: catalog (listing inStock filter), cart (subtotal/availableQty checks), checkout (preview)

contracts.idempotency_rules: Not idempotent. Optional client-supplied Idempotency-Key honored under cross-cutting.idempotency.
Idempotent on orderId. Second call with same orderId + same items returns the original reservation. Different items for the same orderId → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.
failure_modes: PRODUCT_INACTIVE | PRODUCT_DELETED (cross-checked via catalog.product.detail before reserving)
STOCK_NEGATIVE_INVARIANT (concurrent races; should be unreachable but defended by CHECK)
contracts.ordering_guarantees: Per-SKU serialized via row lock; reservations across SKUs in one call are atomic (single tx).

contracts.semantics: sync (also reachable via async event consumption — see payment.completed)
contracts.idempotency_rules: Idempotent on reservationId. Re-committing returns 200 status=COMMITTED.
failure_modes: RESERVATION_EXPIRED (returns 409 — no commit; caller must reissue release flow)
contracts.callers: inventory's own payment.completed consumer (primary). HTTP path retained for ops tooling.

contracts.semantics: sync (also reachable via async event consumption)
contracts.notes: ORD-005 (admin cancel of PAID order) also routes here AFTER reservation has been COMMITTED — in that case 'release' transitions sold→available. Specifically: when the reservation is COMMITTED, release decrements soldQty and increments availableQty by the originally-reserved qty. This handles BA's soft-cancel-of-PAID stock release.

payload_shape.trigger: system_internal: in-process scheduler (gocron / time.Ticker) inside the inventory service. Cadence: every 30 seconds. Not an HTTP endpoint and not exposed on any route; no JWT, no caller — it is a goroutine started at service boot.

scan.query: SELECT id, order_id, sku, qty FROM reservations WHERE status='RESERVED' AND expires_at < NOW() ORDER BY expires_at ASC LIMIT :batch_size FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
scan.rationale: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED prevents two replicas from contending on the same expired row if inventory is scaled horizontally. Batch of 200 keeps each tick's tx short; subsequent ticks drain the backlog.

per_row_action_in_single_tx: 1. SELECT stock_levels FOR UPDATE WHERE sku = reservation.sku
2. UPDATE stock_levels SET reserved_qty = reserved_qty - reservation.qty, available_qty = available_qty + reservation.qty WHERE sku = reservation.sku
3. UPDATE reservations SET status='RELEASED', released_at=NOW(), release_reason='EXPIRED' WHERE id = reservation.id
4. INSERT INTO outbox_events (event_type='reservation.expired', aggregate_id=order_id, payload_json={...}) — see events.reservation.expired
payload_shape.ordering_within_tick: Process rows ORDER BY expires_at ASC so older expirations release first; per-(orderId, sku) writes are serialized by the FOR UPDATE on stock_levels.
payload_shape.no_response: Sweeper has no caller and no response shape. Observability is via logs + metrics (counter: reservations_swept_total{outcome=released|skipped|errored}; gauge: reservations_pending_expiry).
payload_shape.ttl_constant_reference: Reservation expiresAt is set by inventory.reservation.create at now + cross-cutting.pricing.constants.RESERVATION_TTL_MINUTES (15 minutes).

contracts.idempotency_rules: Idempotent by construction. A reservation already in RELEASED or COMMITTED state is filtered out by the WHERE status='RESERVED' clause. If the tick crashes mid-batch, the next tick re-scans uncommitted rows (the FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED does not persist across tx; rows return to the pool).
failure_modes: DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE — sweeper logs and skips the tick; next tick retries. No client-facing failure (no client).
Outbox publisher lag — events.reservation.expired publication is decoupled via outbox; consumers (Order) absorb at-least-once delivery.
contracts.ordering_guarantees: Per-orderId: at most one reservation.expired event ever emitted (the reservation row transitions RESERVED→RELEASED exactly once under the FOR UPDATE row lock). Cross-orderId ordering is not preserved and not required.
contracts.notes: Resolves PR-001 (Option A). Closes the abandoned-checkout stock-leak hole — customer hits checkout.commit, walks away, never simulates: within 15min + sweep-cadence (30s) the reservation is released and Order is notified via events.reservation.expired.

contracts.idempotency_rules: Consumer dedup on eventId via the per-service consumed_events table (same pattern as events.payment.completed).
failure_modes: Order: transition PENDING_PAYMENT → PAYMENT_EXPIRED; write status_history row {fromStatus: PENDING_PAYMENT, toStatus: PAYMENT_EXPIRED, actorRole: SYSTEM, reason: 'reservation expired (TTL)'}. If order is already terminal (CANCELLED, PAYMENT_FAILED, PAYMENT_EXPIRED, PAID, etc.) → idempotent no-op (Order is state-driven; event ignored if current status not PENDING_PAYMENT).

Payment: if a REQUIRES_PAYMENT intent still exists for orderId, transition the intent to EXPIRED and emit events.payment.expired? — NO. To avoid duplicate-cancel cascades, Payment IGNORES events.reservation.expired; the intent simply ages out by its own clock or stays REQUIRES_PAYMENT until a late callback arrives (which then 409s on PAYMENT_INTENT_TERMINAL because Order has already moved). This keeps Payment's outbox cleaner.
contracts.ordering_guarantees: Partition key = orderId. Per-order ordering preserved on consumer side. Cross-topic ordering with ecom.payment.events / ecom.order.events is NOT preserved; consumers (Order, Inventory) MUST be state-driven (read current row state, do not trust event's implicit fromStatus). See events.order.cancelled.failure_modes and events.payment.completed.failure_modes for the disambiguation rule.

contracts.idempotency_rules: Same-SKU adds MERGE into one line (CART-006).

failure_modes: VALIDATION_ERROR (qty>availableQty per CART-002 — must reference availableQty in payload)

contracts.idempotency_rules: Idempotent — removing already-removed line returns current cart.

cart.items: [{cartItemId, productId, sku, name, image, currentPrice, qty, lineSubtotal, availableQty, productStatus, checkoutable}]

contracts.idempotency_rules: Required Idempotency-Key header (CHK-009). Same key + same payload → same orderId. Same key + different payload → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED (returns originally created orderId in error data). Same key still inflight → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INFLIGHT.
failure_modes: INSUFFICIENT_STOCK (CHK-004 — per-item details {productId, requestedQty, availableQty}; no order created)
UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT (inventory or payment unreachable; compensation: release any partial reservation)
internal_orchestration: 2. Resolve buyerEmail: call identity.profile.read using the customer's own Bearer JWT (forwarded from the inbound Authorization header). REQUIRED — feeds order.create-from-checkout's buyerEmail field (REV-L2-001 fix). Failure → 502 + UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT envelope; no state mutated.
4. Validate per-item product status (catalog.product.detail) and stock (inventory.stock.bulk-read) — fast preview check; returns INSUFFICIENT_STOCK pre-commit. No state mutated yet.
5. Begin checkout-tx; persist idempotency_keys row INFLIGHT.
7. Call order.create-from-checkout with X-Internal-Secret + idempotencyKey=newOrderId + buyerEmail (snapshot prices + address; status PENDING_PAYMENT; status_history row).
8. Call payment.intent.create with X-Internal-Secret + idempotencyKey=newOrderId + amount=order.total.
9. Call cart.clear-on-checkout for the moved cartItemIds (CHK-010) — best-effort; failure logs WARN, does NOT roll back.
Compensation matrix (every compensation call carries X-Internal-Secret + the same orderId-as-idempotencyKey; all targets are idempotent):
- failure at step 6 (inventory.reservation.create) → no state mutated; return error.

- failure at step 7 (order.create-from-checkout) → call inventory.reservation.release reason=ORDER_CANCELLED; if release also fails, log CRITICAL + saga DEGRADED; reservation TTL (15min) is the safety net.

- failure at step 8 (payment.intent.create) → call order.cancel-on-checkout-failure THEN inventory.reservation.release reason=ORDER_CANCELLED; on retry-exhaustion log CRITICAL + saga DEGRADED; the events.reservation.expired sweeper path drives PAYMENT_EXPIRED via the Order consumer (REV-L2-004 + REV-L2-008 require both that the consumer is shipped and that a saga reconciler surfaces DEGRADED rows).

Forwarded JWT note: when Checkout calls identity.profile.read in step 2 it forwards the inbound Authorization header (the customer's Bearer access token) — this is the ONE customer-context call in the flow. Steps 6, 7, 8, 9 use X-Internal-Secret only; Checkout does NOT forward the customer JWT into Inventory/Order/Payment because those services trust Checkout's internal-secret and apply their own per-row ownership/idempotency rules.

contracts.idempotency_rules: Optional Idempotency-Key for admin retries. Re-issuing the same (orderId, toStatus) when the row is already at toStatus is a 200 idempotent success (no extra status_history row, no extra event). Default behavior: last-writer-wins guarded by the FOR UPDATE row lock + the transitions table.
failure_modes: INVALID_ORDER_STATE — current row status does not match an allowed fromStatus for requested toStatus per the transitions table (ORD-003 / PR-009 / requirement §9.2)
VALIDATION_ERROR — toStatus=SHIPPED without trackingNumber (ORD-006); toStatus=CANCELLED without reason (ORD-005)
contracts.ordering_guarantees: Server holds SELECT orders FOR UPDATE row lock on the order during the transition to serialize concurrent admin actions and to make the (current-state read → validate → write) sequence atomic.
contracts.side_effects: Writes status_history. For toStatus=CANCELLED (both PENDING_PAYMENT and PAID origins), publishes events.order.cancelled via outbox. For toStatus=SHIPPED, persists trackingNumber on orders.tracking_number.

Second call with the same orderId + same canonicalized body returns the original response. Different body for the same orderId → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED with the original orderNumber in the error data.

VALIDATION_ERROR — buyerEmail missing/malformed; idempotencyKey != orderId; subtotal/total inconsistent with items

Without this contract being formally authored, dry-run #1 had Checkout's outbound struct missing the field and Order's inbound struct requiring it — every commit 400'd at step 7.

contracts.idempotency_rules: Idempotent on orderId: re-cancelling an already-CANCELLED-by-this-path order returns 200 with status=CANCELLED (no extra status_history row, no extra event). Calling on an order that has already moved to PAID (the post-step-8 race where payment success arrived during the compensation window) returns 409 INVALID_ORDER_STATE — Checkout's caller logic must escalate to admin-cancel at that point.

INVALID_ORDER_STATE — order is no longer PENDING_PAYMENT (e.g. event-driven transition raced ahead); see idempotency_rules
contracts.ordering_guarantees: Single tx: SELECT orders FOR UPDATE; if status=PENDING_PAYMENT → transition to CANCELLED, write status_history row (actorRole=SYSTEM, reason from request), publish events.order.cancelled via outbox. The published event carries cancelActor=SYSTEM so Inventory's state-driven consumer applies the standard release branch (RESERVED → available, since Checkout's compensation calls inventory.reservation.release in parallel, the consumer typically sees a no-op).

contracts.side_effects: Writes status_history row, publishes events.order.cancelled via outbox.

Both halves must ship in dry-run #2.

contracts.idempotency_rules: Idempotent on orderId — second call returns the original intent.
First simulate wins. Subsequent simulate calls on a TERMINAL intent return PAYMENT_INTENT_TERMINAL.

contracts.idempotency_rules: STRICT idempotency on (paymentIntentId, providerStatus) — see callback_dedup table. A repeat returns the original applied=true response. A request with the same paymentIntentId but a contradicting providerStatus arriving after a TERMINAL state → 409 PAYMENT_INTENT_TERMINAL with original outcome.
failure_modes: PAYMENT_AMOUNT_MISMATCH (PAY-006: callback amount != intent.amount; intent stays REQUIRES_PAYMENT; order stays PENDING_PAYMENT; reservation untouched)
contracts.ordering_guarantees: First callback per intent wins. Persistence is single-tx: dedup-row insert + payment_records update + outbox event write. Outbox publisher emits payment.completed | payment.failed | payment.expired downstream.
contracts.notes: PAY-005 enforced by dedup_key = sha256(paymentIntentId || providerStatus). Duplicate insert raises a unique-constraint violation that the handler catches and treats as 'replay' → re-emit cached response, NO new outbox event.

contracts.idempotency_rules: Consumers (Order, Inventory) MUST dedupe on eventId. Consumer-side dedup table per-service: consumed_events(eventId PK, consumerName, processedAt). Beyond eventId dedup, consumers are STATE-DRIVEN (see failure_modes) — they read the current row state of the affected aggregate inside the same tx that processes the event and act on actual current state, not on any implicit assumed fromStatus.
failure_modes: consumer transient failure → at-least-once redelivery; idempotency keeps it safe

Order (state-driven): SELECT orders WHERE id=orderId FOR UPDATE; if status=PENDING_PAYMENT → transition to PAID, write status_history, commit. If status is anything else (CANCELLED, PAYMENT_EXPIRED, PAYMENT_FAILED, PAID) → log 'late payment.completed for non-PENDING_PAYMENT order'; do NOT change status; do NOT emit further events. Out-of-scope future enhancement: order.payment-arrived-too-late refund signal.

Inventory (state-driven): SELECT reservations WHERE order_id=orderId FOR UPDATE; do NOT trust any implicit fromStatus on the event. If reservation.status=RESERVED → COMMIT it (decrement reserved, increment sold). If reservation.status=COMMITTED → idempotent no-op. If reservation.status=RELEASED (the customer/admin/sweeper got there first — see PR-003 race) → DO NOT re-reserve, DO NOT re-decrement; log 'payment.completed arrived after reservation released for orderId={orderId}'; emit (informational) inventory.reservation-conflict metric counter. The Order will already have ignored the late payment.completed by the rule above, so the system stays consistent.

race PR-003: concurrent customer order.cancel-mine + payment success. If Inventory consumes payment.completed FIRST (reservation→COMMITTED), then events.order.cancelled (fromStatus=PENDING_PAYMENT) arrives — Inventory reads current state (COMMITTED, not RESERVED) and applies the COMMITTED→RELEASED branch (sold→available), regardless of the event's fromStatus field. Disambiguation = current-row-read, not event payload.
contracts.ordering_guarantees: Partition key = orderId. All payment.* events for one order land on the same partition (topic ecom.payment.events) → strict per-order ordering preserved within this topic. Cross-topic ordering with ecom.order.events and ecom.inventory.events is NOT preserved by Kafka; consumers MUST disambiguate via state-driven reads (see failure_modes).

contracts.idempotency_rules: Consumer dedup on eventId. Consumers are STATE-DRIVEN — they read current aggregate state and do not trust any implicit fromStatus on the event.
failure_modes: Order (state-driven): SELECT orders FOR UPDATE; if status=PENDING_PAYMENT → transition PAYMENT_FAILED, write status_history. Otherwise idempotent no-op (already-cancelled / already-expired / already-paid orders are not retransitioned).

Inventory (state-driven): SELECT reservations FOR UPDATE; if status=RESERVED → release (reserved→available). If status=COMMITTED (payment was earlier successful then a late failed callback raced — should be unreachable due to payment-callback's PAYMENT_INTENT_TERMINAL guard, but defensively) → log + no-op. If status=RELEASED → idempotent no-op.
contracts.ordering_guarantees: Partition key = orderId. Per-order ordering preserved within ecom.payment.events. Cross-topic disambiguation via state-driven reads (see PR-003 race documentation in events.payment.completed).

contracts.idempotency_rules: Consumer dedup on eventId. Consumers are STATE-DRIVEN.
failure_modes: Order (state-driven): SELECT orders FOR UPDATE; if status=PENDING_PAYMENT → transition PAYMENT_EXPIRED, write status_history. Otherwise idempotent no-op. Note: the same PAYMENT_EXPIRED state may also be reached via events.reservation.expired (sweeper path); whichever arrives first wins, the second is a no-op.
Inventory (state-driven): SELECT reservations FOR UPDATE; if status=RESERVED → release (reserved→available). If COMMITTED → defensive log + no-op. If RELEASED → idempotent no-op.
contracts.ordering_guarantees: Partition key = orderId. Per-order ordering preserved within ecom.payment.events. Cross-topic disambiguation via state-driven reads.

contracts.idempotency_rules: Consumer dedup on eventId. Consumers are STATE-DRIVEN — they MUST ignore the event's fromStatus field and instead read the current reservation row by orderId to decide the action. fromStatus is informational/audit only.
failure_modes: Inventory (state-driven; PR-003 race resolution): SELECT reservations WHERE order_id=orderId FOR UPDATE — act on CURRENT state, NOT on event.fromStatus.
- if reservation.status=RESERVED → release (reserved→available); typical PENDING_PAYMENT customer-cancel path

- if reservation.status=COMMITTED → release sold→available (decrement soldQty, increment availableQty by reservation.qty); typical PAID admin-cancel path AND the PR-003 race path where payment.completed was consumed before order.cancelled (event.fromStatus says PENDING_PAYMENT but reality is COMMITTED — current-row-read wins)
- if reservation.status=RELEASED → idempotent no-op (already-released by sweeper, prior cancellation, or a prior payment.failed/expired event)

Payment (state-driven): SELECT payment_intents FOR UPDATE; if status=REQUIRES_PAYMENT → transition to CANCELLED. If TERMINAL (SUCCEEDED, FAILED, EXPIRED, CANCELLED) → no-op. Note: in the PR-003 race where payment succeeded first, intent is already SUCCEEDED, so this branch correctly does nothing — the sold→available release on Inventory is the entire stock-side compensation.
contracts.ordering_guarantees: Partition key = orderId. Per-order ordering preserved within ecom.order.events. Cross-topic ordering with ecom.payment.events / ecom.inventory.events is NOT preserved by Kafka. Disambiguation rule (CANONICAL): Inventory and Order both read current row state inside the consumer transaction and act on actual state, never on event.fromStatus. event.fromStatus is retained in the payload purely for audit/debug.

contracts.idempotency_rules: Consumer (inventory) dedup on eventId. Inventory upserts stock_levels(sku) with all zeros if absent.
contracts.ordering_guarantees: Partition key = sku. Per-SKU ordering preserved.
